lessons.title: What is HTML?
objectives: Understand what HTML is and why it matters
Recognize the basic structure of an HTML document
lessons.content: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language used to structure content on the web. Every website you visit is built with HTML at its core — it tells the browser what each piece of content is: a heading, a paragraph, a link, an image.
lessons.notes: HTML describes structure, not appearance. Styling is CSS's job.
lessons.mistakes: Beginners often try to style pages using HTML attributes instead of CSS — keep structure and style separate.
lessons.practice: Write an HTML snippet with one heading and one paragraph about yourself.
lessons.challenge: Add a second paragraph describing your goal for learning to code.
lessons.code:
Hello WaiTech

I'm starting my coding journey today.

quiz.question: What does HTML mainly describe?
options: The structure and meaning of content

hint.en: Think: which part says 'this is a heading' or 'this is a paragraph'?
hint.sw: Fikiria: ni sehemu ipi inayosema 'hii ni kichwa' au 'hii ni aya'?

explanation.en: HTML tells the browser what each piece of content IS (heading, paragraph, link). Colours are CSS.
explanation.sw: HTML huambia browser kila kipande cha maudhui ni NINI (kichwa, aya, kiungo). Rangi ni kazi ya CSS.

quiz.question: Which language should you use to change the colours and layout of a page?

hint.en: It has 'Style' in its full name: Cascading Style Sheets.
hint.sw: Jina lake kamili lina neno 'Style': Cascading Style Sheets.

explanation.en: CSS handles appearance. Keeping structure (HTML) and style (CSS) separate is a core habit.
explanation.sw: CSS hushughulikia muonekano. Kutenganisha muundo (HTML) na mtindo (CSS) ni tabia muhimu.

quiz.question: What will this show in the browser?
options: Nothing, the code has an error
A big heading, then a paragraph

hint.en: h1 is a heading and p is a paragraph.
hint.sw: h1 ni kichwa na p ni aya.

explanation.en:
makes a main heading and

a paragraph, so you see both, in that order.
explanation.sw:
hutengeneza kichwa kikuu na

aya, kwa hiyo unaona vyote, kwa mpangilio huo.

lessons.title: Document Structure
objectives: Learn the required parts of an HTML document
lessons.content: Every HTML document starts with a doctype declaration, followed by an html element containing a head (metadata) and a body (visible content).
lessons.notes: The doctype tells the browser to render in standards mode.
lessons.mistakes: Forgetting the doctype can cause the browser to render in quirks mode.
lessons.practice: Sketch out a full document structure on paper before typing it.
lessons.challenge: Add a <title> inside the head that names your page.

quiz.question: Which part of an HTML document holds the content people SEE on the page?

hint.en: One part is for 'metadata', the other for what is visible.
hint.sw: Sehemu moja ni ya 'metadata', nyingine ni ya vinavyoonekana.

explanation.en: The <body> contains everything visible. The <head> holds information about the page, like its title.
explanation.sw: <body> ina kila kinachoonekana. <head> ina taarifa za ukurasa, kama kichwa chake (title).

quiz.question: What is the job of <!DOCTYPE html> at the top of the file?
options: It makes the page load faster
It tells the browser to use modern standards mode

hint.en: It is the very first line and it is about how the browser should READ the page.
hint.sw: Ni mstari wa kwanza kabisa na unahusu browser ISOMEJE ukurasa.

explanation.en: Without it, browsers may fall back to 'quirks mode' and render the page in unexpected ways.
explanation.sw: Bila hiyo, browser inaweza kutumia 'quirks mode' na kuonyesha ukurasa kwa njia zisizotarajiwa.

quiz.question: Where does the <title> tag belong?

hint.en: The title is information ABOUT the page (it appears on the browser tab).
hint.sw: Title ni taarifa KUHUSU ukurasa (inaonekana kwenye tab ya browser).

explanation.en: <title> is metadata, so it lives inside <head>. It is shown on the tab, not in the page.
explanation.sw: <title> ni metadata, kwa hiyo iko ndani ya <head>. Inaonekana kwenye tab, si ndani ya ukurasa.

lessons.title: Headings & Paragraphs
lessons.content:
HTML provides six heading levels, h1 through h6, used to create a logical outline of a page. Paragraphs are wrapped in

tags.
lessons.notes: Use only one h1 per page and don't skip heading levels for accessibility.
lessons.mistakes: Using headings purely for large, bold text instead of structure.
lessons.practice: Create an h1 title and two h2 section headings with a paragraph under each.
lessons.challenge: Add an h3 subsection under one of your h2 sections.

quiz.question: Which tag makes the MOST important heading on a page?

hint.en: Smaller number = more important.
hint.sw: Namba ndogo = muhimu zaidi.

explanation.en: <h1> is the top-level heading. Headings go from h1 (most important) to h6 (least).
explanation.sw: <h1> ni kichwa cha juu kabisa. Vichwa huanzia h1 (muhimu zaidi) hadi h6 (kidogo zaidi).

quiz.question: Why should you NOT use <h2> just to make text look big?
options: Headings describe structure, and screen readers use them to navigate

hint.en: Think about someone who listens to the page instead of looking at it.
hint.sw: Fikiria mtu anayesikiliza ukurasa badala ya kuuangalia.

explanation.en: Headings build the page outline. Use CSS for size, and headings for meaning.
explanation.sw: Vichwa hujenga muhtasari wa ukurasa. Tumia CSS kwa ukubwa, na vichwa kwa maana.

quiz.question: Which code puts a paragraph under the heading correctly?

hint.en: Tags must open and close in the right order.
hint.sw: Tags lazima zifunguliwe na kufungwa kwa mpangilio sahihi.

explanation.en:
Each element is opened and closed on its own:

…

then

…

.
explanation.sw:
Kila elementi inafunguliwa na kufungwa yenyewe:

…

kisha

…

.

lessons.title: Links & Navigation
objectives: Create hyperlinks with the anchor tag
Link to external pages and page sections
lessons.content: The <a> tag creates hyperlinks. The href attribute defines the destination — another page, an external site, or an anchor within the same page.
lessons.notes: Always give links descriptive text, not "click here".
lessons.mistakes: Leaving href empty or using javascript:void(0) unnecessarily.
lessons.practice: Create three links: one to an external site, one internal, one to a page anchor.
lessons.challenge: Make a link open in a new tab safely using target and rel attributes.

quiz.question: Which attribute tells a link WHERE to go?

hint.en: It stands for 'hypertext reference'.
hint.sw: Inasimamia 'hypertext reference'.

explanation.en: <a href="…"> sets the destination. src is for images, alt is for image descriptions.
explanation.sw: <a href="…"> huweka mahali kiungo kinapoenda. src ni ya picha, alt ni maelezo ya picha.

quiz.question: Which link text is best for accessibility and SEO?

hint.en: Good link text still makes sense when read alone.
hint.sw: Maandishi mazuri ya kiungo yana maana hata yakisomwa peke yake.

explanation.en: Descriptive text tells people (and search engines) what they will get.
explanation.sw: Maandishi yanayoelezea huwaambia watu (na search engines) watakachopata.

quiz.question: What does target="_blank" do?
options: Opens the link in a new tab

hint.en: The word 'blank' hints at a fresh, empty place.
hint.sw: Neno 'blank' linakumbusha mahali papya, patupu.

explanation.en: _blank opens a new tab. Add rel="noopener" for safety when linking to other sites.
explanation.sw: _blank hufungua tab mpya. Ongeza rel="noopener" kwa usalama unapoweka viungo vya tovuti nyingine.

lessons.title: Images & Media
objectives: Embed images with the img tag
lessons.content: Images are embedded with the self-closing tag. The src attribute points to the file, and alt provides a text description for accessibility and SEO.
lessons.notes: Alt text should describe the image's purpose, not just its contents.
lessons.mistakes: Leaving alt empty on meaningful images breaks accessibility.
lessons.practice: Add an image with a descriptive alt attribute to a sample page.
lessons.challenge: Set explicit width and height attributes to prevent layout shift.

quiz.question: Which tag shows a picture?

hint.en: It is short: three letters.
hint.sw: Ni fupi: herufi tatu.

explanation.en: embeds an image. It has no closing tag (it is self-closing).
explanation.sw: huweka picha. Haina tag ya kufunga (inajifunga yenyewe).

quiz.question: What is the alt attribute for?
options: A text description for screen readers and when the image fails to load

hint.en: Imagine someone who cannot see the picture.
hint.sw: Fikiria mtu asiyeweza kuona picha.

explanation.en: alt describes the image's purpose. It helps accessibility, SEO and shows if the image fails.
explanation.sw: alt huelezea kusudi la picha. Husaidia upatikanaji, SEO na huonekana picha ikishindwa kupakia.

quiz.question: Find the problem in this code.
options: The src attribute is missing, so there is no image

hint.en: How does the browser know WHICH picture to show?
hint.sw: Browser inajuaje ni picha IPI ya kuonyesha?

explanation.en: src points to the image file. Without it, there is nothing to display.
explanation.sw: src huonyesha faili la picha. Bila hiyo, hakuna cha kuonyesha.

lessons.title: Lists
lessons.content: Unordered lists (<ul>) show bullet points; ordered lists (<ol>) show numbers. Both contain <li> items.
lessons.notes: Lists communicate grouping and order to assistive technology, not just visuals.
lessons.mistakes:
Using
instead of proper list markup to fake a list.
lessons.practice: Build a to-do list with five ordered steps.
lessons.challenge: Nest a sub-list inside one of your list items.
lessons.code:
1. Plan the page
  2. Write the HTML
  3. Style with CSS

quiz.question: Which tag creates a list with BULLET points?

hint.en: 'u' stands for 'unordered'.
hint.sw: 'u' inasimamia 'unordered' (bila mpangilio).

explanation.en: <ul> is an unordered (bullet) list. <ol> is ordered (numbered).
explanation.sw: <ul> ni orodha isiyo na mpangilio (vitone). <ol> ina mpangilio (namba).

quiz.question: What goes directly inside <ul> and <ol>?

hint.en: Each entry of the list uses the same tag.
hint.sw: Kila kipengele cha orodha kinatumia tag ile ile.

explanation.en: Each list entry is an <li> (list item).
explanation.sw: Kila kipengele cha orodha ni <li> (list item).

quiz.question: You want steps that must be followed in order (1, 2, 3). Which is best?

hint.en: Order matters here, so choose the numbered list.
hint.sw: Mpangilio una maana hapa, kwa hiyo chagua orodha ya namba.

explanation.en: <ol> shows numbers automatically and tells assistive tech the order matters.
explanation.sw: <ol> huonyesha namba yenyewe na huambia teknolojia saidizi kuwa mpangilio ni muhimu.

lessons.title: Tables
objectives: Structure tabular data with table, tr, td
lessons.content: Tables use <table>, rows use <tr>, and cells use <td>. Header cells use <th> to label columns or rows for assistive tech.
lessons.notes: Tables should be used for real tabular data, never for page layout.
lessons.mistakes: Using tables to lay out entire pages, a common outdated practice.
lessons.practice: Build a 3x3 table of your favorite languages and their use cases.
lessons.challenge: Add a <caption> describing the table's content.

quiz.question: Which tag makes a table ROW?

hint.en: 'tr' = table row.
hint.sw: 'tr' = table row (safu mlalo).

explanation.en: <tr> is a row. Inside it you put cells: <td> for data and <th> for headers.
explanation.sw: <tr> ni safu mlalo. Ndani yake unaweka seli: <td> kwa data na <th> kwa vichwa.

quiz.question: What is <th> used for?
options: A header cell that labels a column or row

hint.en: 'h' stands for 'header'.
hint.sw: 'h' inasimamia 'header' (kichwa).

explanation.en: <th> labels columns or rows, which also helps screen readers.
explanation.sw: <th> huweka jina la safu wima au mlalo, na husaidia pia screen readers.

quiz.question: When is it right to use a table?
options: To place the menu on the left and content on the right
To show real tabular data like a price list

hint.en: Use it only when the information naturally has rows and columns.
hint.sw: Itumie tu pale taarifa ina safu mlalo na wima kiasili.

explanation.en: Tables are for data. Page layout belongs to CSS.
explanation.sw: Majedwali ni ya data. Mpangilio wa ukurasa ni kazi ya CSS.

lessons.title: Forms & Inputs
lessons.content: Forms collect user input using <form> with elements like <input>, <textarea>, and <select>. Each input should have an associated <label>.
lessons.notes: Labels linked with the 'for' attribute improve accessibility and click targets.
lessons.mistakes: Placeholder text is not a replacement for a real label.
lessons.practice: Build a contact form with name and email fields plus a submit button.
lessons.challenge: Add basic validation using the required attribute.

quiz.question: Which tag wraps a whole form?

hint.en: It has the same name as the thing it is.
hint.sw: Ina jina lile lile la kitu chenyewe.

explanation.en: <form> groups the inputs and sends them together when submitted.
explanation.sw: <form> hukusanya inputs na kuzituma pamoja zinapotumwa.

quiz.question: How do you connect a <label> to its input?
options: Match the label's for to the input's id
Put them on the same line

hint.en: Look at the code: 'for' and 'id' share the word name.
hint.sw: Angalia code: 'for' na 'id' vina neno name.

explanation.en: The for attribute must equal the input's id. Then clicking the label focuses the input.
explanation.sw: Attribute for lazima iwe sawa na id ya input. Kisha kubonyeza label kunachagua input.

quiz.question: Why is placeholder text NOT a replacement for a label?
options: It disappears when typing and is not reliably read by screen readers

hint.en: What happens to a placeholder as soon as you start typing?
hint.sw: Placeholder hufanyaje mara unapoanza kuandika?

explanation.en: Labels stay visible and accessible. Placeholders are only hints.
explanation.sw: Labels hubaki zikionekana na zinapatikana. Placeholders ni vidokezo tu.

lessons.title: Semantic Elements
objectives: Use header, nav, main, section, footer
lessons.content: Semantic elements describe the meaning of content, not just its appearance — helping search engines, screen readers, and other developers understand your page.
lessons.notes: A page built entirely from <div> tags loses meaning for assistive technology.
lessons.mistakes: Wrapping everything in generic divs when a semantic tag already exists.
lessons.practice: Rebuild a sample page using header, main, section and footer.
lessons.challenge: Add an <article> for a blog-post style block of content.

quiz.question: Which is a semantic element?

hint.en: It tells you what the content IS just from its name.
hint.sw: Jina lake linakuambia maudhui ni NINI.

explanation.en: <footer> clearly says 'this is the footer'. <div> and <span> have no meaning.
explanation.sw: <footer> inasema wazi 'hii ni footer'. <div> na <span> hazina maana yoyote.

quiz.question: Which tag should hold the MAIN content that is unique to the page?

hint.en: Its name says it all.
hint.sw: Jina lake linaeleza kila kitu.

explanation.en: <main> contains the primary content. Use it once per page.
explanation.sw: <main> ina maudhui ya msingi. Itumie mara moja kwa ukurasa.

quiz.question: Why are semantic tags better than only using <div>?
options: They remove the need for CSS
They help search engines, screen readers and other developers understand the page

hint.en: Think about who else 'reads' your page besides people looking at it.
hint.sw: Fikiria nani mwingine 'anasoma' ukurasa wako mbali na watu wanaouangalia.

explanation.en: Meaningful tags give structure that machines and people can rely on.
explanation.sw: Tags zenye maana hutoa muundo ambao mashine na watu wanaweza kuutegemea.

lessons.title: Building Your First Page
objectives: Combine everything learned into one page
lessons.content: Now you'll combine headings, paragraphs, links, images, lists and semantic structure into one complete personal profile page.
lessons.notes: Real pages are built incrementally — start simple, then layer on structure.
lessons.mistakes: Trying to make it perfect before it's even complete — iterate instead.
lessons.practice: Assemble a one-page personal profile using everything from this module.
lessons.challenge: Add a navigation bar linking to each section of your page.

quiz.question: A link should jump to the section with id="about". Which href is correct?

hint.en: Anchors to an id on the same page start with a special symbol.
hint.sw: Viungo vya id kwenye ukurasa ule ule huanza na alama maalum.

explanation.en: #about points to the element with id="about" on the same page.
explanation.sw: #about huelekeza kwenye elementi yenye id="about" kwenye ukurasa ule ule.

quiz.question: What is the best way to build your first full page?
options: Start simple, then add structure and details step by step
Write everything at once and make it perfect
Copy a page and change nothing

hint.en: Developers work in small steps and check often.
hint.sw: Wasanidi hufanya kazi hatua ndogo ndogo na kukagua mara kwa mara.

explanation.en: Build a small working page first, then improve it. Iterating beats perfection.
explanation.sw: Jenga ukurasa mdogo unaofanya kazi kwanza, kisha uuboreshe. Kuboresha hatua kwa hatua kunashinda ukamilifu.

quiz.question: Where should the navigation links of the page go?

hint.en: There is a semantic tag named for exactly this.
hint.sw: Kuna tag ya semantic iliyopewa jina kwa kazi hii hasa.

explanation.en: <nav> marks the main navigation, and it normally sits in the header.
explanation.sw: <nav> huashiria menyu kuu, na kwa kawaida iko ndani ya header.

lessons.title: ARIA & Accessible Forms
objectives: Build a fully accessible form field
lessons.content: ARIA attributes fill accessibility gaps native HTML can't cover — but native semantic elements should always be your first choice before reaching for ARIA.
lessons.notes: The first rule of ARIA: don't use ARIA if a native HTML element already does the job.
lessons.mistakes: Adding role="button" to a div instead of just using a real <button>.
lessons.practice: Add aria-label to an icon-only button.
lessons.challenge: Connect an error message to an input using aria-describedby.

quiz.question: What should you try BEFORE reaching for ARIA?

hint.en: A real <button> already has the right role.
hint.sw: <button> halisi tayari ina role sahihi.

explanation.en: Native elements give accessibility for free; ARIA only fills gaps.
explanation.sw: Vipengele asilia hutoa ufikivu bure; ARIA hujaza mapengo tu.

quiz.question: What does aria-label="Close menu" do on an icon-only button?
options: Gives screen readers an accessible name

hint.en: The ✕ alone is not meaningful to a screen reader.
hint.sw: ✕ pekee haina maana kwa screen reader.

explanation.en: aria-label provides the name read aloud.
explanation.sw: aria-label hutoa jina linalosomwa kwa sauti.

quiz.question: Which makes a form field accessible?

hint.en: Use for/id.
hint.sw: Tumia for/id.

explanation.en: Labels tell assistive tech what the field is for.
explanation.sw: Label huambia teknolojia saidizi shamba ni la nini.

lessons.title: Meta Tags & SEO Basics
objectives: Write effective title and meta description tags
lessons.content: Meta tags in the head communicate a page's purpose to search engines and social platforms. A good title and description directly affect click-through rates.
lessons.notes: Keep titles under ~60 characters and descriptions under ~155 for search results.
lessons.mistakes: Stuffing meta descriptions with repeated keywords instead of a natural summary.
lessons.practice: Write a title and meta description for a sample course page.
lessons.challenge: Add an Open Graph og:title and og:description tag.
lessons.code:
<title>Learn JavaScript — WaiTech Coding Academy</title>
<meta name="description" content="Interactive JavaScript lessons from beginner to advanced.">

quiz.question: Where do meta tags live?

hint.en: Not visible on the page.
hint.sw: Haionekani kwenye ukurasa.

explanation.en: Head holds page metadata.
explanation.sw: Head ina metadata ya ukurasa.

quiz.question: What does meta name="description" influence?
options: The snippet shown in search results

hint.en: Click-through rate.
hint.sw: Kiwango cha kubofya.

explanation.en: Search engines often show it under the title.
explanation.sw: Injini za utafutaji mara nyingi huionyesha chini ya kichwa.

quiz.question: A good <title> should be:

hint.en: It appears in tabs and results.
hint.sw: Huonekana kwenye tabo na matokeo.

explanation.en: Unique, descriptive titles help users and SEO.
explanation.sw: Vichwa vya kipekee na vinavyoeleza husaidia watumiaji na SEO.

lessons.title: Advanced Form Validation
lessons.content: HTML5 provides built-in validation via attributes like pattern, min, max and required, reducing the need for custom JavaScript validation for common cases.
lessons.notes: Native validation improves accessibility since screen readers understand it automatically.
lessons.mistakes: Relying only on client-side validation without server-side checks in real applications.
lessons.practice: Add a pattern attribute to validate a simple phone number format.
lessons.challenge: Style the :invalid pseudo-class on an input for visual feedback.
lessons.code: <input type="email" required pattern=".+@.+\..+" title="Enter a valid email">

quiz.question: Which attribute makes a field mandatory?

hint.en: Built into HTML5.
hint.sw: Imejengwa ndani ya HTML5.

explanation.en: required blocks submit when empty.
explanation.sw: required huzuia kutuma ikiwa tupu.

quiz.question: What does pattern do?
options: Checks the value against a regular expression

hint.en: A regex.
hint.sw: Regex.

explanation.en: The browser validates input against it.
explanation.sw: Browser huthibitisha ingizo dhidi yake.

quiz.question: Which attributes limit a number input?

hint.en: Shortest names.
hint.sw: Majina mafupi.

explanation.en: min/max set the allowed range.
explanation.sw: min/max huweka kiwango kinachoruhusiwa.

lessons.title: Custom Elements Basics
objectives: Understand what a custom element is
lessons.content: Web Components let you define new HTML tags with encapsulated behavior using the customElements registry — the same low-level API frameworks build on top of.
lessons.notes: Custom element names must contain a hyphen, e.g. <wtca-badge>.
lessons.mistakes: Forgetting the hyphen requirement when naming a custom element.
lessons.practice: Sketch what attributes a <wtca-badge> element might need.
lessons.challenge: Research connectedCallback and describe what it's used for.

quiz.question: What do Web Components let you create?
options: New HTML tags with encapsulated behaviour

hint.en: Like <wtca-badge>.
hint.sw: Kama <wtca-badge>.

explanation.en: Custom elements extend HTML.
explanation.sw: Custom elements hupanua HTML.

quiz.question: Which call registers a custom element?

hint.en: On the customElements registry.
hint.sw: Kwenye registry ya customElements.

explanation.en: define connects the tag name with the class.
explanation.sw: define huunganisha jina la tag na class.

quiz.question: Custom element tag names must:

hint.en: wtca-badge.
hint.sw: wtca-badge.

explanation.en: The hyphen avoids clashes with standard tags.
explanation.sw: Kistari huepuka migongano na tags za kawaida.
